sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Curon Venosta, called Graun im Vinschgau by the municipality, sits on the Reschensee in South Tyrol, and the only source we could read is its register of council and executive decisions, which lists titles and not documents. What follows says what was decided and when, never what the decisions contain. On 9 February 2026 the municipal council approved an ordinance regulating parking, camping and other forms of overnight stay, and on 20 April 2026 the executive set the tariffs for the paid car parks and the exemption permits [0][1]. The council also took a decision on the operation of the municipality's car parks on 29 September 2025 [2]. The fees for the numbered car parks Reschen 13 Piz and Graun 8 Turm were raised by executive decisions in April and May 2022, amending a framework decision of 2021; they may have been replaced by the 2026 decision [3]. No amounts or text were published, so we cannot say what anything costs.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The register shows a series of projects. The executive approved the certificate of proper execution for the redesign and extension of the public car park in Graun, with infrastructure for the bus stop and green areas, on 18 November 2024 [8]. A new public car park on the former ANAS site in Reschen was built in 2023 and 2024, with the certificate of proper execution on 16 September 2024 [9]. The extension of the Maseben car park in Langtaufers was approved as a feasibility project on 28 April 2025 and its final account on 21 September 2026, without a statement on whether the works are finished [10]. In Reschen a bus stop for three line buses at Piz is being arranged, with the project guideline approved on 29 June 2026, the execution project on 7 August 2026 and a mayoral urgency measure on 4 September 2026 [11]. The executive approved the project to demolish and rebuild the Reschen to Piz-Schöneben lift on 28 April 2025 and its first variant on 15 June 2026, and the register does not say whether work has begun [12]. On 27 April 2026 it commissioned a feasibility study for a roundabout at the junction of the SS 40 and the Langtaufererstraße [13]. In May 2026 the executive approved the tender and then the award for the allocation of municipal land for electric-vehicle charging stations, without naming an operator or places [7].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The municipality runs its car parks itself and approves the accounts of the fee collection each year, the one for 2025 on 20 April 2026 [5]. The company Schöneben AG has agreements with the executive on the running of the car park Piz, extended in April 2022 and a new agreement in June 2023; the register gives no terms [4]. The executive bought pay-and-display machines in 2022 and 2024, ordered a repair of the machine at the Turm after a lightning strike in March 2024, and on 29 June 2026 commissioned the extension of the system for electronic payment, without saying whether it is complete [6]. The Turm car park by the sunken church tower has a public toilet with coin machines [14].

Our data cover the Schöneben car park, with 250 spaces, for 25 days since 27 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 25% both on weekdays and at weekends, with a peak of 61% in a single reading early on a Saturday morning. The window falls between the summer season and the winter ski season.
